title: When Morning Begins
logline: In one small town, 'morning' begins at a different hour for the baker, the fisher, the drummer and the farmer.
human_question: Morning, east, today: are these things in the world, or agreements we make with the sun and moon?

premise.story: One night-to-dawn cycle through people whose work defines when 'morning' starts.
premise.place: A town where several dawn trades meet.
premise.experience: The night slowly turning: sounds, lights and people waking in sequence.

concept_links.why: Time- and direction-concepts arise from the movement of sun and moon.
A conventional frame everyone relies on and no one can point to.

possible_arc.opening: Midnight: someone's day is already starting.
possible_arc.turn: Each trade names the hour differently.
possible_arc.ending_open: Sunrise, which is nobody's 'morning' in particular.

requirements: Several dawn trades within reach of each other

suggestions.name: Kandy, around the dawn drumming at the Temple of the Tooth
suggestions.why: Drums mark the hour for a whole city.
suggestions.verify: Filming permissions at the temple are strict.

suggestions.name: A southern fishing harbour (e.g. Mirissa or Beruwala)
suggestions.why: Boats return at dawn; markets start in the dark.
suggestions.verify: Access, permissions and current conditions are unverified.

risks: A montage with no single human thread
drop_if: No person to carry the night
unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
